prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In a top-down view of a workshop floor, the depth map highlights the camera wearer's torso and outstretched arms as the brightest regions (0.2–0.7 m away) directly below the viewpoint, reaching into a round trash bin resting on the floor about 0.8–1.2 m ahead and slightly to the right. Around the bin at roughly 1.2–2.0 m distance, medium-grey silhouettes mark a green lawnmower immediately behind the bin (about 0.3 m from its rim) and cluttered workshop equipment, crates, and tools to the left and right (1.5–2.5 m apart), while a second person standing and then crouching near the upper-left background is 2.5–3.5 m away and 1.5–2.5 m left of the lawnmower. Across the five frames, the wearer steps slightly closer to the bin in frames 2–4 before turning slightly leftward in frame 5, while the background person at the top-left shifts from standing upright to crouching down toward the floor mats in frame 4 and lifting a mat within their arm's reach in frame 5, facing away or sideways and never looking toward the camera wearer. The depth map clearly separates the vertical height of the raised bin rim, the recessed interior contents, and the wearer's reaching right arm—which partially occludes the bin opening—more distinctly than the cluttered RGB image. However, the map is unreliable along the dark upper floor where the second person's legs and crouching body blend nearly into the black floor background, and in frame 1 where equipment on the far left appears artificially brighter and closer than its true floor distance.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the camera wearer's lower torso, legs, and arms at the bottom of each frame (0.2–0.8 m away, within immediate arm's reach of the bin in front) and detects the second person in the upper-left background (2.5–3.5 m from the wearer and roughly 2.0 m left of the central lawnmower) across all five frames. As the sequence progresses, the wearer's mask shifts rightward and upward as the right arm reaches into the trash bin (0.8–1.2 m ahead) in frames 2–4 and retreats slightly in frame 5, while the upper-left person's small mask tracks them moving from standing (frames 1–3, cropped at the upper-left frame boundary) to crouching facing left/downward (frame 4) and holding a floor mat (frame 5) without ever facing the camera wearer. While this map makes it easy to track the two human figures against the busy workshop floor at a glance, it completely fails to segment any of the prominent surrounding objects—missing the trash bin within the wearer's reach, the cardboard piece held in the right hand, the green lawnmower 1.5 m ahead, and the tool crates on the left. Furthermore, the segmentation is highly unreliable: in frame 2 it merges the cylindrical trash bin into the wearer's green 'person' mask and splits the wearer's right arm into a separate 'person' instance, in frame 4 it fragments the cardboard box inside the bin as a tiny blue 'person' sliver, and in frame 5 it misclassifies a long tool handle on the left (1.8 m away) as a 'skateboard' while splitting the wearer's arms and torso into separate 'person' masks.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders only 2D hand skeletons in magenta on a black background, consistently detecting the camera wearer's left hand hovering above the lower-left torso at about 0.4–0.5 m from the camera across all five frames. It captures the wearer's right hand (0.6–0.8 m away, to the right of and slightly below the left hand in image space) only in frame 3 as it grasps the cardboard inside the trash bin and in frame 5 as it reaches into the bin's left side, while completely missing the right hand in frames 1, 2, and 4 where the hand is angled edge-on or partially occluded by the cardboard and frame border. The map shows the precise finger curl and palm orientation of the wearer's left hand throughout the slight torso turns and of the right hand during grasping, which are harder to parse against the similarly toned floor and bin clutter in RGB. However, it is severely incomplete for broader spatial layout: it detects no yellow body skeletons for either the camera wearer (whose torso and legs are cropped at the bottom boundary) or the second person 2.5–3.5 m away in the upper-left background (who faces away/sideways and crouches to reach the floor mats), and provides no representation of the surrounding workshop objects or their relative distances.
